name: Household
judgment_calls: Unmarried co-adopters are two taxpayers under the statute's words: each has a $17,280 cap and a $5,000 refundable amount. §23(i) only authorises regulations; shown as a variant.
In the shared-limit variant the one $17,280 is freely divisible between the two; (a)(4) is not shared because §23(i) does not name it.
A joint return is one taxpayer: one cap, one $5,000.
Head of household is open to the unmarried adult who claims the child, never both; §2(b)/§152 tests assumed met (not in the reading list).
Baseline is the best one-payer position, so the gain isolates the split.
The refundable $5,000 comes out of the credit first, before the §26(a) limit.
Tax from the rate schedule to the cent, no tax-table rounding.
silences: §23 gives no rule for how non-spouse co-adopters share the (b)(1) or (a)(4) amounts; (i) leaves (b)(1) to regulations and omits (a)(4).
§23 does not require the child to be the claimant's dependent.
The listed text does not say whose payment it is when one adult funds the other's payment.
§23(c) carryforward base read as written: only the subpart A (nonrefundable) portion.
Five-year carryforward limit not modelled (single year).
